topics.title: AI data centers put power bills in focus
topics.summary: U.S. officials expanded a voluntary pledge meant to keep AI data center growth from raising household electricity bills, while some lawmakers are looking at stronger grid-cost rules.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a giant tech project needs a ton of electricity, who should pay for the upgrades: the company, customers, or everyone a little bit?

topics.title: Central U.S. heat keeps hanging on
topics.summary: Forecasters say a broad heat dome is keeping dangerous temperatures across much of the central and southern U.S., with humidity and warm nights making the stretch harder on people.
topics.discussionPrompt: When summer heat gets stubborn, what is your best low-effort cooling strategy: shade, cold drinks, errands later, or fully surrendering to air conditioning?

topics.title: Canada debates stronger wildfire response
topics.summary: Canada's active wildfire season has renewed calls for a national emergency agency, while federal officials continue tracking regional fire danger and support needs across provinces and territories.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would a big national wildfire team make you feel more prepared, or do local crews still know the land best?

topics.title: Two meteor showers peak tonight
topics.summary: The Southern Delta Aquariids and Alpha Capricornids are peaking around July 30, offering late-night skywatchers a chance at fast streaks and occasional bright fireballs despite moonlight.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you had ten quiet minutes under the night sky, would you hunt for meteors or immediately start ranking constellations by personality?

topics.title: Japan assesses Kyushu quake damage
topics.summary: After a magnitude 7.1 quake hit southern Japan, officials reported damaged roads, disrupted trains and safety checks, while residents were urged to stay alert for the next few days.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a city is checking bridges, trains and power after a quake, what would you want updated first: maps, transit, phones, or snack supplies?
